e43.title: Demo nested epic: program
e43.body: Public demo of a tree three levels deep, used by epic-pulse fixtures and live tests.

source.body:
## Summary
- A sub-issue with its own sub-issues is followed as a **sub-epic**, at every level down to GitHub's limit of eight. The VS Code view opens each sub-epic onto its own status groups, with its own `40% · 2/5`.
- An epic now counts the **leaves** of its whole tree, not its direct children: a sub-epic with ten tasks weighs ten, not one. A dropped sub-epic counts as one dropped item.
- A refresh walks the tree a level per round, so a new tree arrives in one refresh. Sub-epics refresh every 6 minutes (top epic every 2) to stay inside the 300-point hour.
- Cost: the query asks each child for its sub-issue count; GitHub bills **5 points per epic** (was 4). Confirmed live: the demo refresh costs 11 (1 + 2×5).
- `epic-pulse json`: children gain `subCount`, `counts`, `percent` and their own `children` (additive).

## Safety
- A hierarchy that loops back stops where it repeats; 8 levels and 2000 nodes are the backstop. The view and the refresh use the same depth limit (I found and fixed an off-by-one where the deepest fetched sub-epic was never shown).

## Verification
- Real recordings of a three-level demo tree I created in this repo (#43 → #44 → #45 → #48, plus #46 and closed #47).
- lint, typecheck, 480 tests; live 483 pass.
- Mutation-verified: cycle stop, leaf counting, sub-epic TTL, pruning of sub-epics, depth cap.

## Not verified
- Not looked at in a running VS Code. None of the real AnypointConnect epics I checked (#6509, #6217, #6243, #5684) has sub-epics today, so on that repository this changes only the cost and nothing visible.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
